cases.computed_description: orthonormal spatial triad adapted to V.
cases.name: b2.observer_frame_is_orthonormal_and_spatial
cases.notes: the triad supplies coordinates ON the design space; it is never used to extract physics FROM a tensor, which is what made the quarantined legacy tetrad path unsound
cases.reference: the spatial triad satisfies g_lab(e_i, e_j) = delta_ij and g_lab(e_i, V) = 0

cases.name: b2.observer_frame_orthonormality
cases.reference: g_lab(e_i, e_j) = delta_ij and g_lab(e_i, V) = 0

cases.name: b2.parameter_vector_roundtrip
cases.notes: pins the parameter ordering. A silent reordering would leave every other case passing while the reported design meant something else
cases.reference: q -> coefficients -> q is the identity, and q -> blocks -> coefficients likewise, for every linear family

cases.name: b2.symmetry_by_construction
cases.notes: EXACT zero, not a tolerance: both (i,j) and (j,i) read the same parameter, so there is nothing to cancel
cases.reference: eps and mu^-1 are symmetric and zeta_adjoint = zeta^T for every family, with no symmetrisation step applied afterwards

cases.name: b2.spatiality_by_construction
cases.reference: every block is spatial with respect to V, structurally

cases.name: b2.reconstructed_tensor_is_reciprocal
cases.notes: the design space is reciprocal by construction, so J_reciprocity is a diagnostic and not a useful optimizer term
cases.reference: Z_design^{abcd} = Z_design^{cdab} for every family

cases.name: b2.a11_reconstruction_roundtrip
cases.notes: the optimizer drives the SAME reconstruction B1C verified; there is no second production formula
cases.reference: design blocks -> Z via (A11) -> blocks via (A7) returns the design blocks

cases.name: b2.norms_agree_in_the_analogue_configuration
cases.notes: which is why the coordinate-basis norm is usable there, and why calling it invariant would still be wrong
cases.reference: with g_lab = eta and V = (1,0,0,0) the observer Gram is the identity, so the coordinate-basis and observer-referred norms coincide exactly

cases.name: b2.observer_referred_norm_is_invariant
cases.notes: G = g_lab + 2 V(x)V transforms as a (0,2) tensor, so the full contraction is a scalar. g_lab alone would be indefinite and the norm could vanish for Z != 0
cases.reference: ||Z||^2_V is unchanged by a nontrivial linear coordinate change

cases.name: b2.coordinate_basis_norm_is_not_invariant
cases.notes: asserted, so the distinction cannot quietly rot into a claim of invariance
cases.reference: the coordinate-basis norm DOES change under the same coordinate change, which is why it is labelled a coordinate-basis norm

cases.name: b2.objective_zero_at_exact_target
cases.notes: the residuals are squared, so the tolerance is the square of the reconstruction accuracy
cases.reference: J_Z and J_blocks vanish when the design equals the target

cases.name: b2.objective_positive_away_from_target
cases.reference: J_Z is strictly positive for every perturbed design

cases.name: b2.objective_is_exactly_quadratic
cases.notes: (A11) is homogeneous linear in the blocks and the blocks are linear in q. This is why centred differences of J carry no truncation error and why the normal-equation reference is the exact minimiser
cases.reference: J_Z is an exact quadratic in q for the linear families: its third difference along any direction vanishes

cases.name: b2.gradient_manufactured_analytic
cases.reference: for J = sum c_k (q_k - a_k)^2 the centred difference reproduces the hand-derived 2 c_k (q_k - a_k)

cases.name: b2.oti_gradient_manufactured_matches_analytic
cases.notes: this is the case that tests the seeding and batch assembly against a CLOSED FORM. It is deliberately independent of the constitutive objective, so a failure names the AD plumbing rather than the physics
cases.parameters: 21 parameters in 7 batches of at most 3
cases.reference: the batch-assembled HyPAD gradient of J = sum c_k (q_k - a_k)^2 equals the hand-derived 2 c_k (q_k - a_k) exactly

cases.name: b2.gradient_finite_difference_matches_analytic
cases.notes: the objective is exactly quadratic, so this comparison is not step-size limited in the usual way
cases.reference: centred differences of J_Z reproduce 2 A_k . (A q - z) / s, the gradient implied by the linear design map

cases.name: b2.oti_gradient_matches_analytic
cases.notes: tighter than the finite-difference comparison by three orders of magnitude, because neither side is differenced
cases.reference: the batch-assembled HyPAD gradient of J_Z equals the closed-form 2 A_k . (A q - z) / s implied by the linear design map

cases.name: b2.oti_gradient_is_batched
cases.notes: the backend is onumm3n2 with three derivative directions. An interface claiming to seed 21 at once would be a lie about it
cases.reference: the 21-parameter gradient is assembled from batches of at most kOtiDirections = 3 active directions

cases.name: b2.oti_gradient_matches_finite_difference
cases.notes: the objective is not reimplemented for the AD scalar: evaluate_design is instantiated at OTIScalar and called unchanged
cases.reference: the batch-assembled HyPAD gradient equals the centred-difference gradient of the same objective

cases.name: b2.oti_gradient_batch_independence
cases.notes: catches derivative directions leaking into each other, which a comparison against finite differences alone would blur
cases.reference: a partial derivative is identical whether its parameter was seeded alone or alongside two others

cases.computed_description: target: reciprocal; pair-antisymmetric; finite; observer-decomposable; metric-induced. J: 2.7186e-02 -> 6.8098e-21, relative |Z_design - Z_target| = 1.4297e-10, ObjectiveBelowTolerance
cases.name: b2.recovery.metric_induced
cases.notes: compared against Z_target, NOT against another observer's Plebanski blocks. That comparison is the one B1C withdrew
cases.reference: a subluminal Alcubierre effective metric with g_lab = eta is recovered in the unrestricted reciprocal family, compared against Z_target itself

cases.expected_description: nonzero residual, matching the normal-equation solution
cases.name: b2.restricted_family_is_a_projection_not_a_fit
cases.notes: the residual is a property of the family, not an optimizer failure. The reference is dense Gaussian elimination on the normal equations, written in the test and not calling the optimizer
cases.reference: against a magnetoelectric target, the zeta == 0 family leaves a STRICTLY NONZERO residual, and the optimizer finds the same point as the exact least-squares projection

cases.computed_description: J_Z = 1.7450e-01, penalty = 2.2031e-05, max|eps| = 1.5001e+00 against bound 1.5, entry bound active: yes, MaxIterationsReached
cases.expected_description: nonzero J_Z with the entry bound respected and reported
cases.name: b2.infeasible_bounded_reports_best_approximation
cases.notes: the failure mode this guards against is a gate that reports convergence while the design silently violates its own bounds. The penalty is SOFT by construction -- a smooth hinge admits a small violation in exchange for differentiability -- so max|eps| settles just above the bound rather than exactly on it, and the case allows that explicitly rather than pretending the constraint is hard.
cases.reference: with bounds excluding the target, the result is a BEST BOUNDED APPROXIMATION: J_Z stays strictly positive, the bound is reported as active, and no exact realization is claimed

cases.computed_description: primed target reciprocal; pair-antisymmetric; finite; observer-decomposable; not metric-induced. J -> 9.5999e-21, relative |Z'_design - Z'_target| = 1.0971e-10, ObjectiveBelowTolerance
cases.name: b2.coordinate_change_consistency
cases.notes: the final tensor relationship is what is asserted, NOT an identical iteration history: a coordinate-basis norm reweights the parameters and need not preserve the trajectory
cases.reference: optimizing entirely in the transformed coordinates reconstructs the transformed target: the FINAL TENSOR RELATIONSHIP holds

cases.name: b2.deterministic_repeatability
cases.notes: bit equality, not a tolerance. The perturbation uses a fixed integer recurrence rather than a random engine, so there is no seed to lose
cases.reference: two runs from the same initialization are BIT-IDENTICAL in history, termination reason and final parameters

cases.expected_description: NonFiniteEncountered, and evaluation reports finite = false
cases.name: b2.nonfinite_is_rejected_not_absorbed
cases.notes: an optimizer that silently absorbs a NaN reports convergence to nothing
cases.reference: a non-finite design is rejected with reason NonFiniteEncountered, and an overflowing design is reported as not finite rather than silently scored

cases.name: b2.target_classification_is_recorded
cases.notes: a target that failed reciprocity would be reported, not silently fitted: the design space is reciprocal, so the achievable residual would then be bounded below by the target's own skewon part
cases.reference: a metric-induced target is classified as metric-induced, reciprocal, pair-antisymmetric, finite and observer-decomposable
